chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Let not one of you lengthen his moustache, for indeed Satan takes it as a hiding place to conceal himself by.'
ai.seo_question: Why should Muslims avoid lengthening their moustache according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) conveys the Prophet’s (PBUH) instruction to trim the moustache, attributing the prohibition to Satan using the lengthened hair as a 'hiding place' (makhbarran) for concealment. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on physical grooming as a manifestation of spiritual purity and a means of distinguishing believers from the influence of Shaytan, linking outward appearance to inner ethical discipline.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Not one of you should lengthen his moustache, for the Satan<sup>la</sup> takes it as a hideout to hide by’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘You must not allow your mustache to grow long; Satan makes it his hiding place and cover.’”
